headline: Lakes are temporary features—bowls of water that glaciers, tectonics, and time create and destroy
universal_truth: Even bodies of water that seem permanent are slowly changing or disappearing
fun_facts: Most lakes are less than 15,000 years old—babies in geological time
Lake Baikal in Russia holds 20% of the world's unfrozen freshwater in a single lake
Lakes naturally fill with sediment and vegetation over time; without intervention, they become wetlands, then land
discussion_questions: What 'lakes' in your life—things that seem permanent—might be temporary?
How does knowing lakes disappear change how you value them?
What would happen if all lakes vanished?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A lake seems eternal—sitting there, still and permanent. But lakes are geological newcomers. Most are younger than human civilization. And every lake is slowly filling with sediment, destined to become meadow and then forest. Lakes are just pauses in water's journey.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: If water flows downhill and eventually reaches the ocean, why do lakes exist at all? What creates these bowls that hold water temporarily on its way to the sea?

options.text: Glaciers, volcanoes, or tectonic activity create depressions that fill with water
options.response: Yes. Something must create the bowl—glaciers carving, volcanoes collapsing, earth shifting.

options.text: Rivers slow down in flat areas and spread out into lakes
options.response: Rivers can widen, but true lakes need something else...

q1.title: Glacial Sculptors
q1.script: Most lakes in temperate regions were carved by glaciers during the last ice age—only 15,000 years ago. Massive ice sheets gouged depressions, then melted and filled them. The Great Lakes are glacier footprints filled with their own melted ice.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Glacial Sculptors"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Lake Baikal's Treasure
q2.script: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the oldest and deepest lake on Earth—25 million years old and 5,387 feet deep. It holds 20% of the world's unfrozen freshwater. One lake, containing more freshwater than all five Great Lakes combined.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Lakes Die
q3.script: Every lake is dying from the moment it's born. Sediment washes in. Plants grow. The lake slowly becomes a wetland, then a meadow, then a forest. Without dredging, even the grandest lake is just a very slow-motion pond.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What seems permanent is often just slow. Lakes remind us that stillness is temporary, that all containers eventually fill, and that what looks eternal is just changing at a pace we can't perceive.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 57. Tomorrow, we'll explore life in the desert. Until then, if you see a lake, appreciate its temporary beauty.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Temporary Treasures - Value What Won't Last
growTrack.learning_objective: Appreciate things precisely because they're temporary
growTrack.activity: Identify something in your life that seems permanent but is actually slowly changing—a relationship stage, a life phase, a situation. Acknowledge its impermanence. Does knowing it won't last forever change how you experience it today?
